newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end down, hurt by futures traders.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end down, hurt by futures traders.

text.p: South African shares ended Tuesday firmly down as futures traders, mindful of the Friday close-out date on near-dated June contracts, pushed the market into negative territory, dealers said.
The market started slightly off, but as more derivatives players entered the spot market prices soon began to tumble further as they rushed to settle positions.
The all-share index lost 79.4 points to 7,192.1 as the industrials index dropped 49.7 points to 8,432.7.
Golds ended off 28.4 points, or 2.5 percent, to 1,100.5.
Hamstrung by the futures players, the market ignored positive external factors such as softer-than-expected U.S. inflations figures.

Dealers said the local market was also navel-gazing at its own internal factors and sentiment is being stymied by concerns over the looming relaxation of exchange controls on July 1, and attendent capital flight fears.
Another negative factor is renewed fears over a weakening rand that on Tuesday was edging through the 4.50 to the dollar level. It was last quoted at 4.5090/5085 on the U.S. currency.
Individual shares had a mixed day with 123 stocks advancing, against 235 falling. Thirty sunk to new lows while 21 hit new highs.
Overall the market saw a healthy 825 million rands worth of shares exchanging hands.
Dealers said the market was expected to continue on its downward trend all week until the futures close-out date was firmly out of the way.
